profiles.title: Director
profiles.summary: Set the outcome, acceptable risk and accountable owner.
profiles.contribution: Choose the service boundary and the conditions for further investment. Leave unresolved decisions visible.
profiles.artifact: Outcome brief with scope, risk owner and decision criteria.
questions: Which user outcome justifies this investment?
Which consequence must remain under human control?
reviewQuestions: Does the evidence support the proposed scope?
Who can stop the service when the assumptions fail?

profiles.title: Product and delivery manager
profiles.summary: Connect the user outcome to a deliverable that the team can review.
profiles.contribution: Define the first useful scope, dependencies and decisions that need an owner.
profiles.artifact: Delivery plan with acceptance conditions and named handoffs.
questions: Which user problem will the first release address?
What will this release deliberately leave unresolved?
reviewQuestions: Does every release condition have an evidence owner?
Can the team complete the human review work this design creates?

profiles.title: Business analyst
profiles.summary: Make the rules and information sources precise enough to test.
profiles.contribution: Translate interviews and documents into traceable rules, examples and open questions.
profiles.artifact: Rule register linked to sources and acceptance examples.
questions: Which source authorizes this rule?
What happens when two sources disagree?
reviewQuestions: Can a reviewer trace each rule to a decision owner?
Have division-specific exceptions survived the translation?

profiles.title: Domain expert
profiles.summary: Explain the exceptions and judgments that experienced staff use.
profiles.contribution: Provide real task patterns and fictionalized examples that expose undocumented rules.
profiles.artifact: Reviewed examples with exceptions, source authority and unresolved interpretations.
questions: Which unwritten exception would a new colleague miss?
What would make a plausible answer wrong here?
reviewQuestions: Does the proposed rule preserve the original conditions?
Does the fallback send the case to someone who can decide?

profiles.title: Product and service designer
profiles.summary: Make the service understandable when it answers, asks or fails.
profiles.contribution: Define the user journey, accessible controls and recovery from ambiguous or partial outcomes.
profiles.artifact: Interaction flow with examples of normal, uncertain and failed states.
questions: What does the user need to know before accepting this action?
How can the user correct a mistaken assumption?
reviewQuestions: Can the user distinguish a draft from a completed action?
Can someone finish the task without dragging on the canvas?

profiles.title: Engineer
profiles.summary: Turn rules into explicit component boundaries and executable checks.
profiles.contribution: Define contracts, state changes and data dependencies before choosing additional infrastructure.
profiles.artifact: Architecture and implementation brief linked to rules and tests.
questions: Which component enforces each rule?
What happens if this operation succeeds but its response is lost?
reviewQuestions: Does authorization occur at the execution boundary?
Can the proposed tests fail when the rule is violated?

profiles.title: Junior engineer
profiles.summary: Make one small part of the design concrete and reviewable.
profiles.contribution: Trace a worked example through the system, implement a bounded change and explain the evidence to a reviewer.
profiles.artifact: Small implementation task with input, expected result and failing-first test.
questions: Which rule does this task implement?
Which uncertainty should I bring to my reviewer before I code?
reviewQuestions: Can I reproduce the expected failure without a model call?
Have I kept the example and the approved requirement distinct?

profiles.title: QA and test engineer
profiles.summary: Find evidence that can disprove a claim about the system.
profiles.contribution: Define risk slices, boundary cases and independent expectations for deterministic and model-based behavior.
profiles.artifact: Evaluation plan with case lineage, thresholds and regression evidence.
questions: What result would show that this rule is broken?
Which cases must remain outside optimization?
reviewQuestions: Do the measures use the correct denominator?
Were failures retained rather than hidden by retries?

profiles.title: DevOps engineer
profiles.summary: Make builds and deployments repeatable within the agreed boundary.
profiles.contribution: Specify artifact versions, configuration, access controls and the path to restore a known release.
profiles.artifact: Deployment plan with reproducible artifacts and recovery checks.
questions: Which configuration belongs to each environment?
How will we restore a compatible application and data version?
reviewQuestions: Can a clean environment reproduce the release?
Are credentials absent from public files and exported specifications?

profiles.title: Site reliability engineer
profiles.summary: Connect service objectives to observable user outcomes and recovery.
profiles.contribution: Define service signals, alert ownership, incident actions and feedback from production.
profiles.artifact: Operating plan with service objectives, runbook and rollback triggers.
questions: Which failure would users notice before our alerts?
What evidence tells the responder to stop automatic actions?
reviewQuestions: Does the service objective include the human review queue?
Can the responder identify the affected model, rules and corpus?

profiles.title: Finance and commercial partner
profiles.summary: Test whether the proposed outcome is worth its complete operating cost.
profiles.contribution: Make volume, review effort, failure costs and commercial assumptions explicit.
profiles.artifact: Cost model with a defined successful outcome and sensitivity cases.
questions: What counts as a successful outcome in the cost denominator?
Which cost grows when the service abstains or retries?
reviewQuestions: Does the comparison include people and infrastructure?
Who owns an assumption that has not been measured?

tutorial.title: Choose a useful outcome
tutorial.lesson: Begin with a user task and a consequence. State the boundary before choosing a model. All support-assistant examples in this guide are fictional.
tutorial.prompt: What should the user be able to complete?
tutorial.example: A customer identifies the correct reset procedure for an Acme Home Hub without advice intended for the Business Hub.
tutorial.doneWhen: A named owner can explain the intended outcome and the first release boundary. Unknown targets remain marked as unknown.

tutorial.title: Capture the needs and exceptions
tutorial.lesson: Describe the people, context and failure consequences. Include users who need an alternative channel or an accessible interaction.
tutorial.prompt: Which need must the service satisfy first?
tutorial.example: A customer must receive instructions for their exact product version. An unknown model triggers a clarification question.
tutorial.doneWhen: Each need has an actor, an observable result and an example of a wrong result.

tutorial.title: Agree rules and source authority
tutorial.lesson: Record what must happen, the source that authorizes it and who resolves conflicts. A document being newer does not automatically make it authoritative.
tutorial.example: For Home products, use the current approved Home manual. A superseding safety bulletin overrides the affected procedure. Unresolved source conflicts go to product support.
tutorial.doneWhen: Rules have source references, division scope and expected exception outcomes. Unconfirmed interpretations remain open decisions.

tutorial.title: Connect the rules to components
tutorial.lesson: Start with the smallest design that can enforce the rules. Add storage, queues or separate services when a stated requirement needs them.
tutorial.prompt: Where will this rule be enforced?
tutorial.example: One application service validates the product, filters authorized documents, retrieves evidence and drafts the reply. Account changes use a separately authorized tool.
tutorial.doneWhen: Each selected component has a purpose, a contract and links to the rules it implements. The diagram remains a proposed design until reviewed.

tutorial.title: Define the evidence
tutorial.lesson: Use reviewed examples with explicit measures and decision criteria. Separate development examples from the held-out cases used for a release comparison.
tutorial.prompt: What observation would make us reject this design?
tutorial.example: A test asks for Home Hub instructions while the index contains a similar Business Hub procedure. Any cross-division source in the answer fails this case.
tutorial.doneWhen: Cases cover ordinary tasks, risk slices and failures. Measures, proposed thresholds, dataset roles and evidence owners are explicit.

tutorial.title: Prepare release and operation
tutorial.lesson: Record the release evidence, the person who decides and the recovery path. Completed fields do not establish readiness.
tutorial.prompt: What evidence must the release owner review?
tutorial.example: The release owner reviews source-filter tests, held-out answer results, capacity checks and a rollback rehearsal before deciding whether to enable a limited pilot.
tutorial.doneWhen: The release decision, remaining unknowns, cost assumptions and operating ownership are recorded. Approval is explicit and tied to a version.

tutorial.title: Hand off a reviewable specification
tutorial.lesson: Export the agreed scope with traceable rules, acceptance cases and unresolved questions. An agent may propose an implementation; it cannot approve its own design.
tutorial.prompt: What bounded task should the next person or agent perform?
tutorial.example: Implement the division filter and its tests. Keep the source-conflict policy unresolved and do not deploy the assistant.
tutorial.doneWhen: The recipient can identify the project revision, authorized task, acceptance evidence and decisions they must return to a person.

checkpoints.title: Outcome and scope
checkpoints.purpose: Agree why the service exists and what this version may attempt.

questions.label: Which user outcome will this version improve?
questions.hint: Describe a completed task that a person can observe.
questions.example: Customers identify the correct reset procedure for their Home Hub version.

questions.label: What is outside this version?
questions.hint: Name exclusions that change the design or the promise to users.
questions.example: The assistant cannot diagnose electrical faults or change account details.

questions.label: Who owns the decision to proceed?
questions.hint: Name the accountable role and the current decision state.
questions.example: The support director owns the pilot decision; approval is pending.

questions.label: How does the current service perform?
questions.hint: Record evidence or an unknown rather than an assumed improvement.
questions.example: Current completion rate is unknown; the support manager will review a representative sample.

questions.label: What spending boundary applies to the pilot?
questions.hint: State the unit and whether the amount is proposed or approved.
questions.example: A fictional monthly cap of EUR 500 is proposed; finance approval is pending.

checkpoints.title: Source authority and conflicts
checkpoints.purpose: Keep rules linked to evidence that an accountable person accepts.

questions.label: Which sources may define product behavior?
questions.hint: Name the document family and responsible owner.
questions.example: The Home product owner maintains the approved Home manuals and safety bulletins.

questions.label: Which source takes precedence for this rule?
questions.hint: Use an explicit precedence rule rather than popularity or retrieval rank.
questions.example: A safety bulletin that explicitly supersedes a manual section takes precedence for that section.

questions.label: What happens when applicable sources conflict?
questions.hint: Specify an outcome that does not silently choose a winner.
questions.example: The assistant states that the sources conflict and routes the question to Home support.

questions.label: How is an authoritative revision identified?
questions.hint: Capture approval state and applicability as well as a version label.
questions.example: The corpus accepts manuals marked approved with a product version and an effective period.

questions.label: Which interpretation still needs a decision?
questions.hint: Name the unresolved point and the person who must decide.
questions.example: The treatment of regional reseller leaflets is unknown; the Home product owner must decide.

checkpoints.title: Product and division routing
checkpoints.purpose: Send each request to evidence and people authorized for its context.

questions.label: Which divisions require separate handling?
questions.hint: Use distinctions that affect policy or access.
questions.example: Home and Business products have separate procedures and support teams.

questions.label: What evidence identifies the applicable product?
questions.hint: Specify the trusted input rather than an inference from wording alone.
questions.example: The customer selects the product model; signed-in account metadata can prefill the choice.

questions.label: What happens when the product is uncertain?
questions.hint: Define a clarification or escalation outcome.
questions.example: Ask the customer to choose a model; do not combine Home and Business procedures.

questions.label: Who receives a request that cannot be routed?
questions.hint: Identify a reachable fallback owner.
questions.example: The general support queue receives the case with the unresolved product field.

questions.label: Which example exposes incorrect routing?
questions.hint: Include a case where similar wording could hide a different rule.
questions.example: A Business Hub request must not use a Home Hub reset guide with the same error-code text.

checkpoints.title: Data access and freshness
checkpoints.purpose: Define which data the service may use and how changes reach its answers.

questions.label: Who may read each source category?
questions.hint: Name the permission boundary and enforce it before retrieval returns content.
questions.example: Public manuals are readable by all; tenant tickets require verified membership of that tenant.

questions.label: What freshness does this source require?
questions.hint: State a task-specific target and its decision status.
questions.example: The proposed target is to reflect an approved safety bulletin within one hour; the owner must confirm it.

questions.label: What happens when freshness cannot be established?
questions.hint: Choose a visible fallback instead of implying current evidence.
questions.example: The assistant stops procedural advice for that product and links the staffed support channel.

questions.label: How does a revoked source stop appearing?
questions.hint: Include indexes and cached results in the removal path.
questions.example: A revocation invalidates source-tagged chunks and answer caches before further responses use them.

questions.label: Which request content may the service retain?
questions.hint: Specify the minimum data and the authority for its retention.
questions.example: Retain task category and result codes; the permitted retention of message text is still unknown.

checkpoints.title: Rules and exception outcomes
checkpoints.purpose: Make tacit expertise visible through observable examples.

questions.label: What must happen when this condition is true?
questions.hint: Write one condition and its required outcome.
questions.example: If the model version is unknown, ask for the label before giving reset instructions.

questions.label: Which exception do experienced staff apply?
questions.hint: Capture a practice that a new colleague could miss.
questions.example: A device with a reported burning smell goes directly to the safety procedure instead of the reset flow.

questions.label: What happens when evidence is insufficient?
questions.hint: Separate an unknown answer from a negative answer.
questions.example: State that the available manual does not answer the question and offer a support handoff.

questions.label: Which case is closest to the rule boundary?
questions.hint: Use a concrete example that reviewers can adjudicate.
questions.example: A user reports warmth during normal operation but no smell; the domain expert must define the relevant distinction.

questions.label: Who can approve a change to this rule?
questions.hint: Separate a suggested interpretation from an authorized revision.
questions.example: The product safety owner approves safety-rule changes; agent suggestions remain drafts.

checkpoints.title: Actions and human approval
checkpoints.purpose: Make consequential state changes explicit before the service can request them.

questions.label: What external state can this action change?
questions.hint: Describe the effect in user terms.
questions.example: A replacement request creates an order against the customer account.

questions.label: Which action requires explicit approval?
questions.hint: Identify the decision, authorized approver and scope.
questions.example: A customer must approve the exact replacement item and delivery address before submission.

questions.label: What must the approval be bound to?
questions.hint: Prevent a later change from reusing an earlier approval.
questions.example: Bind approval to the account, item, address and draft revision; editing any field requires a new approval.

questions.label: What happens after a retry of the same action?
questions.hint: Define the result when the first attempt may already have succeeded.
questions.example: Reuse the request identifier and return the existing order rather than creating another.

questions.label: What does cancellation mean after partial success?
questions.hint: Distinguish stopping work from reversing a completed effect.
questions.example: Stop later steps and report the created order; cancellation of the order follows its own authorized process.

checkpoints.title: Architecture and component contracts
checkpoints.purpose: Give each component a rule to implement and a boundary that can be tested.

questions.label: Which need justifies this component?
questions.hint: Start with a requirement before choosing infrastructure.
questions.example: The retrieval component supplies approved passages for the selected product.

questions.label: What input does the component accept?
questions.hint: Name required fields and the treatment of absent values.
questions.example: A retrieval request needs tenant scope, product ID and question; missing product ID returns a clarification outcome.

questions.label: What output does the component promise?
questions.hint: Include enough identity to trace an answer to its source.
questions.example: Return passage text with document ID, revision, section and access scope.

questions.label: What failure outcome must the caller handle?
questions.hint: Use explicit states rather than an empty success-shaped value.
questions.example: An unavailable index returns an unavailable status; zero matches returns no evidence.

questions.label: Which requirement justifies an additional service?
questions.hint: Record uncertainty if scaling or isolation needs are unmeasured.
questions.example: A separate ingestion worker is proposed because document updates exceed the interactive request budget; load evidence is pending.

checkpoints.title: Evaluation cases and decision criteria
checkpoints.purpose: Connect claims to checks that can fail and evidence that people can review.

questions.label: Which reviewed example tests this rule?
questions.hint: Specify the input, expected outcome and source revision.
questions.example: For a Home Hub v2 request, only the approved v2 manual may support the reset answer.

questions.label: Which task groups need separate results?
questions.hint: Include important failure costs even when the group is uncommon.
questions.example: Report Home, Business, unknown product, conflicting sources and safety exceptions separately.

questions.label: Which examples remain held out?
questions.hint: Keep optimization, regression and final comparison roles explicit.
questions.example: Develop prompts on the development set; reserve an independently reviewed set for the release comparison.

questions.label: What does the score count?
questions.hint: Name numerator, denominator and treatment of ineligible cases.
questions.example: Retrieval hit rate counts eligible questions with at least one relevant top-five passage; it is not passage recall.

questions.label: Which result would block release?
questions.hint: State proposed thresholds with the responsible decision owner.
questions.example: The proposed contract gate permits zero observed cross-tenant disclosures; this does not prove a zero population failure rate.

questions.label: How will automated judgments be checked?
questions.hint: Define independent labels and a process for disagreement.
questions.example: Domain reviewers adjudicate a calibration set and audit disagreements before judge scores influence release decisions.

checkpoints.title: Cost per successful outcome
checkpoints.purpose: Compare designs using complete costs and an explicit definition of success.

questions.label: What counts as a successful outcome?
questions.hint: Use a user result rather than tokens, responses or closed tickets alone.
questions.example: A customer completes the correct procedure without a later correction within the declared observation window.

questions.label: Which costs belong in the numerator?
questions.hint: Include model use, infrastructure, review work and recovery effort.
questions.example: The pilot records inference, hosting, document maintenance, human review and support rework.

questions.label: Which volume assumptions drive the estimate?
questions.hint: Separate observed traffic from a planning scenario.
questions.example: A fictional scenario assumes 1000 requests per month; observed pilot traffic is not yet available.

questions.label: What is the estimated cost per successful outcome?
questions.hint: Label estimates and show the calculation.
questions.example: Illustrative only: EUR 400 total cost divided by 800 successful outcomes gives EUR 0.50 per outcome.

questions.label: Which uncertain input could change the decision?
questions.hint: Test a different review or failure rate rather than one precise forecast.
questions.example: Recalculate if the fraction of cases needing staff review doubles.

questions.label: Who decides when spending exceeds the agreed limit?
questions.hint: Specify a decision owner and the service response.
questions.example: The product manager pauses expansion and asks finance to review the cap before further rollout.

checkpoints.title: Release evidence and decision
checkpoints.purpose: Make the release decision reviewable against a specific system version.

questions.label: Which system revision is under review?
questions.hint: Include model, prompt, corpus, rules and application versions.
questions.example: The candidate references application r7, prompt p3, corpus c4 and rule register r2; the model revision is recorded in its manifest.

questions.label: Where is the acceptance evidence?
questions.hint: Link results and retain failures with their disposition.
questions.example: The release record links contract tests, held-out results by slice and the rollback rehearsal.

questions.label: Which decisions remain unresolved?
questions.hint: Keep unknown distinct from accepted risk or approval.
questions.example: The source-refresh target is unconfirmed; the release owner must resolve it before procedural advice is enabled.

questions.label: What release decision has the authorized owner made?
questions.hint: Record approved, rejected or pending with the reviewed revision.
questions.example: Pending: the support director has not yet approved this candidate.

questions.label: What observation triggers rollback?
questions.hint: Name a condition the operator can detect and an available response.
questions.example: A confirmed tenant-boundary violation disables retrieval and starts the incident procedure.

questions.label: What is the initial exposure boundary?
questions.hint: Describe the permitted pilot population and capabilities.
questions.example: The proposed pilot serves volunteer staff with public manuals and no order-creation tool.

checkpoints.title: Incident response and recovery
checkpoints.purpose: Help the responder contain harm and preserve enough evidence to explain it.

questions.label: What signal starts the incident process?
questions.hint: Prefer an observable user consequence over a vague quality concern.
questions.example: A confirmed answer uses another tenant's ticket content.

questions.label: Who leads the response?
questions.hint: Name an available role and escalation path.
questions.example: The on-call service owner leads; the support manager coordinates affected-user handling.

questions.label: What can the responder disable immediately?
questions.hint: Choose a bounded action that limits further harm.
questions.example: Disable private-ticket retrieval while retaining a clear support fallback.

questions.label: Which evidence is necessary for investigation?
questions.hint: Record versions and identifiers while minimizing private content.
questions.example: Preserve request ID, access decision, source IDs and deployment manifest in the restricted incident record.

questions.label: What evidence permits restoration?
questions.hint: Require a check of the affected boundary before resuming service.
questions.example: The owner reviews the repaired authorization test and a scoped replay before restoring private retrieval.

checkpoints.title: Production feedback and rule change
checkpoints.purpose: Turn operating evidence into reviewed improvements without contaminating independent evaluation.

questions.label: Which production cases will be reviewed?
questions.hint: Define the sample and distinguish representative monitoring from targeted investigation.
questions.example: Sample ordinary requests separately from flagged safety and source-conflict cases.

questions.label: Which observation suggests a change is needed?
questions.hint: Separate user preference, task failure and source drift.
questions.example: Customers repeatedly correct product identification even though the answer wording is rated helpful.

questions.label: What change is proposed in response?
questions.hint: State the hypothesis before editing the rule or prompt.
questions.example: Add explicit model confirmation before retrieval and compare incorrect-routing outcomes.

questions.label: How will these examples be used?
questions.hint: Give each example a role and avoid relabeling exposed cases as untouched.
questions.example: Reviewed incidents become regression cases; a separately collected set measures the revised design.

questions.label: Who can accept the proposed policy change?
questions.hint: Keep feedback and generated suggestions separate from authorization.
questions.example: The product owner reviews the change; its status remains proposed until the decision is recorded.

questions.label: What result would justify keeping the change?
questions.hint: Connect quality to user effort and operating cost.
questions.example: Keep confirmation if routing errors fall enough to justify the extra interaction and support effort under the agreed criteria.

outputs: Versioned policy decision and regression cases

collaborations.title: Split a reviewable implementation
collaborations.question: What is the smallest implementation that proves the selected need and rule together?
collaborations.artifact: Bounded engineering task with acceptance evidence and dependencies.

collaborations.title: Make the task safe to pick up
collaborations.question: Which unresolved assumption should the junior engineer escalate rather than fill in?
collaborations.artifact: Starter task with a named reviewer and explicit stop questions.

collaborations.title: Plan evidence alongside delivery
collaborations.question: Which acceptance cases must exist before the feature can be called complete?
collaborations.artifact: Delivery checklist linked to test and evidence owners.

collaborations.title: Prepare a releasable slice
collaborations.question: Which configuration or environment dependency could prevent this slice from reaching the pilot?
collaborations.artifact: Release dependency plan with environment readiness evidence.

collaborations.title: Include operating work in scope
collaborations.question: Which support obligation does this release create that the delivery plan has not funded?

collaborations.title: Set a measurable pilot budget
collaborations.question: What spending cap buys enough evidence to decide whether the pilot should expand?
collaborations.artifact: Pilot budget with an evidence objective and pause condition.

collaborations.title: Capture the unwritten rule
collaborations.question: Which condition changes the expected answer even though the current procedure does not mention it?
collaborations.artifact: Tacit-rule example awaiting approval from its policy owner.

collaborations.title: Translate rules into interactions
collaborations.question: Which clarification question distinguishes the rule branches without asking for unnecessary data?
collaborations.artifact: Rule-to-interaction mapping with example customer wording.

collaborations.title: Define the contract precisely
collaborations.question: Which rule distinction would disappear if absent, empty and unknown values shared one representation?
collaborations.artifact: Field contract with explicit missing-value semantics.

collaborations.title: Trace a rule through an example
collaborations.question: Can the junior engineer follow this example from source clause to expected output without inventing a condition?
collaborations.artifact: Annotated source-to-test walkthrough for one rule.

collaborations.title: Challenge rule boundaries
collaborations.question: Which neighboring input should produce a different result under this decision table?
collaborations.artifact: Boundary-case table with independently stated expectations.

collaborations.title: Preserve policy by environment
collaborations.question: Which policy settings must be promoted together to keep the released rule consistent?
collaborations.artifact: Rule configuration manifest with environment-specific values.

collaborations.title: Make policy failures observable
collaborations.question: Which result code would let operations distinguish missing evidence from a source conflict?
collaborations.artifact: Rule outcome taxonomy linked to operational signals.

collaborations.title: Specify chargeable outcomes
collaborations.question: Which contractual definition changes whether a completed response counts as a successful service outcome?
collaborations.artifact: Commercial-rule mapping with a cost denominator definition.

collaborations.title: Make exceptions understandable
collaborations.question: How should the assistant explain a safety escalation without implying that it has diagnosed the product?
collaborations.artifact: Domain-reviewed exception message and next action.

collaborations.title: Resolve source precedence
collaborations.question: Which source wins when an approved manual and an applicable superseding bulletin disagree?
collaborations.artifact: Precedence contract with conflict and supersession examples.

collaborations.title: Teach the misleading case
collaborations.question: Which plausible answer should the junior engineer deliberately make a test reject?
collaborations.artifact: Expert-reviewed counterexample for a first regression test.

collaborations.title: Calibrate human judgments
collaborations.question: Which disputed answer should reviewers examine to agree what adequate support means?
collaborations.artifact: Adjudicated rubric example with the original disagreement retained.

collaborations.title: Keep sources current
collaborations.question: What event tells the deployment process that a product document must replace or revoke an indexed revision?
collaborations.artifact: Document publication and revocation handoff.

collaborations.title: Recognize harmful drift
collaborations.question: Which new product behavior would make yesterday's acceptable answers unsafe today?
collaborations.artifact: Domain drift trigger with an operational escalation owner.

collaborations.title: Price the exception workload
collaborations.question: Which complex cases require specialist time that an average handling-cost estimate would hide?
collaborations.artifact: Exception categories with measured or unknown review effort.

collaborations.title: Keep approval attached to the action
collaborations.question: How will the interface and API prevent an edited draft from reusing an earlier approval?
collaborations.artifact: Approval-state contract with revision-binding examples.

collaborations.title: Implement accessible recovery
collaborations.question: How can a keyboard user correct the selected product and return to the same task?
collaborations.artifact: Accessible recovery scenario with a focused implementation task.

collaborations.title: Test comprehension after failure
collaborations.question: Can a user tell whether an interrupted action changed external state?
collaborations.artifact: Usability test for draft, submitted and partially completed outcomes.

collaborations.title: Design the deployment interruption
collaborations.question: What should customers see while an incompatible release or maintenance step prevents service?
collaborations.artifact: Maintenance and degraded-service interaction contract.

collaborations.title: Show useful progress
collaborations.question: Which progress state can the interface truthfully display while a request waits for human review?
collaborations.artifact: User-visible state map linked to measured queue events.

collaborations.title: Account for user effort
collaborations.question: Which cheaper technical option creates extra customer steps or support rework?
collaborations.artifact: Cost comparison that includes interaction effort and recovery work.

collaborations.title: Review a small change together
collaborations.question: Which boundary test demonstrates that the junior engineer's change implements the intended rule?
collaborations.artifact: Reviewable change with a failing-first test and explanation.
